content.rendered:
4:05 p.m. The Senate adjourned and will reconvene at 3:00 p.m. on Monday, September 28. They will resume consideration of S. 4668, the Protect College Sports Act and vote on passage of the bill at 5:30 p.m.

During wrap-up:

H.R. 9340- Ratepayer Protection Act. Second reading and placed on the calendar.

Passed by unanimous consent:

  • S. 3257-John A. Hauser Mental Health in Aviation Act with a Hoeven substitute amendment
  • S. 3258-Aviation Medication Transparency Act of 2026
  • Motion to Concur in the House amendment to S.283 – Illegal Red Snapper and Tuna Enforcement Act
  • H.R.2388 – Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe Project Lands Restoration Act
  • Motion to Concur in the House amendment to S.240 – Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act of 2025

The following resolutions were agreed to en bloc:

  • S.Res.902 – Telehealth Awareness Week
  • S.Res.903 – Nuclear Weapons Workers Day of Remembrance
  • S.Res.904 – Gold Star Families Week
  • S.Res.905 – Lobster Day

3:35 p.m. Senators Warner, Schatz and Kim spoke about AI.

3:15 p.m. Senator Warnock paid tribute to his departing Chief of Staff.

2:53 p.m. Senator Duckworth paid tribute to to her departing staffer, Kalina Thompson.

2:40 p.m. Senator Fischer spoke about the Farm Bill.

2:39 p.m. By a vote of 49-50, the Senate did not adopt H.Con.Res.89 – War Powers Resolution (Iran).

  • GOP Senators in favor: Collins, Murkowski, Paul, and Tillis
  • Senator Fetterman (D) voted no.
  • Senators not voting: Alsobrooks .

1:45 p.m. The Senate began a roll call vote on the adoption of H.Con.Res.89 – War Powers Resolution (Iran).

1:41 p.m. Senator Kaine spoke on the war with Iran.

1:32 p.m. Senator Baldwin spoke on diesel.

1:20 p.m. Senators Klobuchar and Murphy spoke about the Iran war powers resolution.

1:10 p.m. Senator Merkley spoke about Chinese authoritarianism and the freedom of speech. He asked for unanimous consent to proceed to and pass S. 226. Senator Paul objected.

12:57 p.m. Senators Slotkin and Moreno spoke about Chinese cars.

12:43 p.m. Senators Kim and Schiff spoke about the Iran war powers resolution.

12:40 p.m. By a vote of 74-25 the motion to invoke cloture on S. 4658 (Protect College Sports Act) was agreed to. Voting no: Alsobrooks, Blumenthal, Blunt Rochester, Booker, Duckworth, Gillibrand, Hirono, Kaine, Kelly, Kim, Markey, Merkley, Moody-R, Murphy, Paul-R, Reed, Sanders, Schiff, Schumer, Scott-FL-R, Van Hollen, Warnock, Warren, Whitehouse, and Wyden. Senator Tillis did not vote.

11:46 a.m. The Senate began voting on the motion to invoke cloture on S.4658, the Protect College Sports Act.

11:45 a.m. By a vote of 77-23, the Senate adopted the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668 (Protect College Sports Act). Senators voting no: Alsobrooks, Blumenthal, Blunt Rochester, Booker, Duckworth, Gillibrand, Hirono, Kaine, Kelly, Kim, Markey, Merkley, Moody-R, Murphy, Paul-R, Reed, Sanders, Schiff, Schumer, Scott-FL-R, Van Hollen, Warnock, and Warren.

10:47 a.m. The Senate began a roll call vote on adoption of the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668 (Protect College Sports Act).

10:46 a.m. Senator Barrasso made a motion to table amendment #6779 to S.4668 (Protect College Sports Act) and it was agreed to by voice vote. Senator Barrasso then made a motion to table amendment #6777 to S.4668 and it was agreed to by voice vote. Senator Barrasso received unanimous consent for the Senate to vote on adoption of H.Con.Res.89, War Powers Resolution (Iran), at 1:45 p.m. today.

10:30 a.m. Minority Leader Schumer spoke on the White House press ban.

10:15 a.m. Majority Leader Thune spoke on the economy and cost of living.

10:03 a.m. Senator Grassley spoke on fraud prevention.

10:00 a.m. The Senate has convened. Leadership time is reserved and the Senate has resumed consideration of the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, the college sports bill, post-cloture.

The Senate will convene at 10:00 a.m. and resume consideration of the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, the college sports bill, post-cloture.

At 10:45 a.m., the Senate will proceed to two votes:

  1. Adoption of the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment.
  2. Cloture on S.4668, the college sports bill, as amended, if amended.

Further votes are expected.

7:28 p.m. The Senate stands adjourned until 10:00 a.m. tomorrow and in honor of the late Senator Jon Kyl. With Leader Remarks reserved, the Senate will immediately resume consideration of the Cruz-Cantwell amendment #6776 to S.4668.

Votes scheduled: At 10:45am, on Thursday, September 24th, the Senate will proceed to two roll call votes on the following:
1. Motion to invoke cloture on Cal. #449, S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026, as amended, if amended.
2. Adoption of Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to Cal. #449, S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026.
Additional votes are possible.

  • Confirmed by unanimous consent: Cal #918, #119, and PN769-2 Wade E. Arnold on the Secretary’s Desk in the Coast Guard.
  • Received its first reading: H.R. 9430 – American Drone Manufacturing Dominance Act of 2026
  • Passed by UC: S. 1962 -Secure Space Act of 2026. as amended.
  • Passed by UC: S. 3404, – Satellite Cybersecurity Act of 2025, as amended.
  • Agreed to by S. Res. 863 – A resolution expressing support for designation of the week of September 13 through 19, 2026, as “National Adult Education and Family Literacy Week”
  • Agreed to by UC en bloc: S. Res. 888, S. Res. 892, S. Res. 893, S. Res. 894, S. Res. 895, S. Res. 896
  • Agreed to by UC: S. Res. 897 – Honoring the life and legacy of former Senator Jon Kyl of Arizona

7:21 p.m. Senator Lummis wrapped up.

6:40 p.m. Senator Bennet spoke on vaccine schedules for children.

6:09 p.m. Senator Sullivan spoke on his bill related to fishing and bycatch reduction. He then asked unanimous consent to pass S.4938, as amended by the Sullivan amendment at the desk; Senator Markey reserved the right to object and spoke on fisheries. Senator Markey then objected.

5:51 p.m. Senator Whitehouse spoke on climate change and wildfires and asked unanimous consent to take up and pass S. Res. 559; Senator Scott of Florida objected.

5:40 p.m. Senator Blumenthal asked unanimous consent to pass H.R.2550; Senator Scott-Fl objected.

5:37 p.m. Senator Kaine spoke on federal workers.

5:35 p.m. Senator Alsobrooks spoke on federal workers.

5:34 p.m. Senator Blumenthal spoke on federal workers.

5:05 p.m. Senator Hickenlooper spoke on the war with Iran.

4:11 p.m. Senator Schatz spoke on AI.

4:02 p.m. Senator McCormick spoke on the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia and AI.

3:42 p.m. Senator Blackburn spoke on dating site scams and achieved unanimous consent for passage H.R. 2481, Romance Scam Prevention Act.

3:32 p.m. Senator Justice spoke on childhood cancer and achieved unanimous consent for passage of S.2933, a bill to redesignate a playground in the New River Gorge National Park and Preserve in the State of West Virginia as the “Hearts of Gold Playground: In Honor of West Virginia Children and Families Impacted by Childhood Cancer”.

3:23 p.m. Senator Lujan spoke about the New Mexico Land Grant and Cooperation Act and achieved unanimous consent for passage of S.1363, New Mexico Land Grant-Mercedes Historical or Traditional Use Cooperation and Coordination Act, as amended.

3:17 p.m. Senator Shaheen spoke on China’s support of Iran.

3:16 p.m. By a party-line vote of 50-47, the Senate confirmed Angela Veronica Colmenero to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas.

  • Not voting: Senators Daines, Ernst and Tillis.

2:16 p.m. The Senate began a roll call vote on confirmation of Executive Calendar #828, Angela Veronica Colmenero to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas.

2:15 p.m. The Senate returned from recess.

12:43 p.m. The Senate recessed until 2:15 p.m.

12:26 p.m. Senators Marshall and Cassidy spoke on the cost of health care and asked unanimous consent to take up and pass S. 2355, on that topic. Senator Paul objected.

11:54 a.m. Senator Lee spoke on election security and asked unanimous consent to take up and pass S. 5271, on this topic. Senator Padilla asked UC to modify the request to take up and pass S. 5390. Senator Lee objected to the modification, and Senator Padilla objected to the initial request.

11:46 a.m. Senator Ernst spoke on college sports. She then spoke on critical minerals and military supply chains. Senator Ernst then received unanimous consent to pass H.R.1721 – Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act.

11:35 a.m. Senator Coons spoke on college sports.

11:19 a.m. Senator Durbin spoke on DACA students.

11:00 a.m. Senator Paul spoke about college sports. He then made an unanimous consent request to call up his amendment #6758 to S. 4668; Senator Barrasso objected.

10:49 a.m. Senator Barrasso spoke about China.

10:41 a.m. Senator Schumer spoke about the retirement AFSCME president Lee Saunders. He also spoke about China and AI and also tariffs and farmers.

10:22 a.m. Senator Thune spoke about socialism.

10:05 a.m. Senator Grassley spoke about the Working Families Tax Cut.

10:00 a.m. The Senate convened.

The Senate will convene at 10:00 a.m. and resume consideration of Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to Cal. #449, S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026, post-cloture.

The Senate will recess from 12:30 p.m. until 2:15 p.m. for the weekly conference meetings.

At 2:15 p.m., the Senate will proceed to a roll call vote on confirmation of Executive Calendar #828, Angela Veronica Colmenero, of Texas, to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas. Please note, further roll call votes are possible during Wednesday’s session of the Senate.

8:00 p.m. The Senate stands adjourned and will convene at 10:00am on Wednesday to resume consideration of Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to Cal. #449, S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026, post-cloture. The Senate will recess from 12:30pm until 2:15pm for the weekly conference meetings. At 2:15pm, the Senate will proceed to a roll call vote on confirmation of Executive Calendar #828, Angela Veronica Colmenero, of Texas, to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas.

Please note, further roll call votes are possible during Wednesday’s session of the Senate. 

In today’s session of the Senate:

Roll Call Votes

Motion to invoke cloture on Executive Calendar #828, Angela Veronica Colmenero, of Texas, to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas. Invoked (52-43)

Motion to invoke cloture on Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to Cal. #449, S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026. Invoked (70-21)

Wrap Up

S.Res.870- Hispanic Heritage Month

S.Res.871- National Purple Heart Recognition Day H.R.4467 – Vicksburg National Military Park Boundary

7:33 p.m. Senator Scott-Fl spoke on immigration.

7:32 p.m. By a vote of 70-21, the Senate invoked cloture on the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776, to S. 4668. Senators not voting: Cassidy, Coons, Gallego, Kim, Murphy, Schatz, Tillis, Tuberville, and Whitehouse. Senators voting no: Alsobrooks, Blumenthal, Blunt Rochester, Booker, Duckworth, Durbin, Gillibrand, Kaine, Kelly, Markey, Merkley, Moody (R), Paul (R), Reed, Sanders, Schiff, Schumer, Scott-FL (R), Van Hollen, Warnock, and Warren.

6:38 p.m. The Senate began voting on cloture on the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776, to S. 4668, the Protect College Sports Act.

6:36 p.m. By a party-line vote of 52-43, the Senate invoked cloture on the Colmenero nomination. Senators not voting: Cassidy, Coons, Gallego, Murphy and Whitehouse.

5:41 p.m. The Senate began voting on cloture on the nomination of Angela Colmenero to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas.

5:29 p.m. Senator Cruz spoke o the sports bill.

5:20 p.m. Senator Cantwell spoke on the Save our Sports Act.

5:02 Senator Kelly spoke on AI.

4:43 p.m. Senator Tuberville spoke on gender identity.

4:42 p.m. Senator Barrasso received unanimous consent for the following time agreements:

  1. If cloture is invoked on the Colmenero nomination that all post-cloture time be expired and, that the Senate vote on confirmation at a time to be determined by the Majority Leader no later than Friday, September 25.
  2. If cloture is invoked on the Cruz-Cantwell Substitute Amendment #6776 to S. 4668, that all time during adjournment, recess, morning business, and leader remarks count towards post-cloture.

4:25 p.m. Senator Murray spoke on the economy.

4:18 p.m. Senator Wicker spoke on the impending visit of Chinese President Xi. He then spoke on human rights in China.

3:57 p.m. Senator Budd paid tribute to the departing Director of the Marine Corps Senate Liaison Office, Colonel Robert Sucher. He then spoke on the visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping.

3:39 p.m. Senator Durbin spoke on free press in America and Pastor Ezra Jin.

3:24 p.m. Minority Leader Schumer spoke on AI and Iran.

3:09 p.m. Majority Leader Thune spoke on Democrat policies in California.

3:04 p.m. Senator Grassley spoke on ethanol.

3:00 p.m. The Senate convened.

******

The Senate will convene at 3:00 p.m. and following any Leader remarks will resume consideration of the nomination of Angela Veronica Colmenero to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas.

At 5:30 p.m. the Senate will vote on the motion to invoke cloture on the Colmenero nomination.

Further votes are possible during today’s session.

*****

Sports bill: S.4668: Cloture has been filed on S.4668, the sports bill and the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment (6776) to S.4668.

The Senate began the Rule 14 process of placing the following bill directly on the Calendar:

  • A bill to ratify and approve all authorizations, permits, verifications, extensions, biological opinions, incidental take statements, and any other approvals or orders issued pursuant to Federal law necessary for the establishment and administration of the Coastal Plain oil and gas leasing program, and for other purposes. (S.5438)
  • A bill to establish the National Fraud Enforcement Division of the Department of Justice. (H.R.9576)
